fan_analyst.note: Hittin' Season and the Phillies Show both celebrate the rotation's historic turnaround and Harper's MVP-level play, while flagging real concern over Bohm's struggles and Aiden Miller's back injury.

radio_populist.note: Talk-radio host (WIP Daily) captures growing excitement from callers — 'baseball might be back on' — while voicing frustration with Brad Keller and anxiety over Bohm's continued unplayability.

themes.name: Rotation renaissance is real
themes.sample: From worst ERA in baseball under the previous manager to best in baseball since the change — Christopher Sanchez's eight-inning, ten-strikeout gem headlined a stretch of historically dominant starting pitching that has become the engine of the entire turnaround.

themes.name: Harper carrying the offense
themes.sample: Nine home runs, an OPS pushing .950, and a barrel rate at its highest since his MVP season — Bryce Harper is producing at an elite level and has become the undisputed offensive anchor while Schwarber and Bohm continue to struggle.

themes.name: Bohm situation reaching a tipping point
themes.sample: Described as 'unplayable' by multiple observers and pulled mid-game by Don Mattingly, Alec Bohm's prolonged slump is creating real lineup tension and forcing difficult decisions about Edmundo Sosa's role and playing time.

themes.name: Mattingly honeymoon holding — but questions linger
themes.sample: Eight wins in nine games have generated genuine goodwill toward the interim manager, and his refusal to cave to Harper's public push for Stott against lefties earned respect — but his long-term status and whether this run is sustainable remain open questions.

themes.name: Aiden Miller injury alarms prospect pipeline
themes.sample: The top prospect still not swinging a bat in early May, with no detailed public update on his back condition, has raised serious fears about losing another year of development — echoing the Andrew Painter situation — in an organization that has repeatedly struggled to develop position players.

quotes.text: Baseball season? Might be back on in Philadelphia.
quotes.source_hint: talk-radio host (WIP Daily), reacting to the comeback win over the A's

quotes.text: He's an everyday player. When you have a guy that needs to play every day, lefty, righty, it don't matter.
quotes.source_hint: Bryce Harper quote relayed on Hittin' Season, stumping for Bryson Stott

quotes.text: This is extremely worrisome. Your top prospect, a guy you've refused to trade... still not swinging a bat.
quotes.source_hint: fan analyst (Hittin' Season) on Aiden Miller's back injury

quotes.text: The Brad Keller pointless 94 mile an hour change up to a left-handed hitter... one of the single most miserable experiences as a Philadelphia sports fan.
quotes.source_hint: talk-radio host (WIP Daily) venting about the bullpen's weak link

vibe_summary: A four-game winning streak and the most dominant starting pitching stretch in years have Phillies fans genuinely re-engaged, though Bohm's unplayability and a worrying silence around the top prospect keep optimism cautious rather than euphoric.
reasoning: The dominant sentiment driver is the stunning rotation turnaround — statistically from worst to best in baseball since the managerial change — combined with Harper's MVP-caliber run, which has converted genuine despair into cautious excitement. The talk-radio perspective is more emotionally effusive ('baseball is back'), while the fan analyst perspective is more measured, carefully noting that the schedule has softened and real structural concerns remain. Postseason belief stays low because the enthusiasm is grounded in relief and recent momentum rather than confident projections of a deep October run, and the 8.5-game deficit in the division is repeatedly acknowledged.
